identity.operation: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput creates root parsers and calls ParseOneInput; that helper computes an unsigned-long SipHash value from the bytes, calls XML_SetHashSalt, then calls XML_Parse. The entry later creates and parses child parsers.
identity.condition: For finite valid XML input with a nonzero derived SipHash value, XML_SetHashSalt writes zero to the upper key word, writes the value to the lower word, and sets the salt flag. XML_Parse then skips automatic salt generation. Internal hashing copies that limited key.

assessment.requirement: Parser hashing on the target's parse and external-entity surface must be able to use a full 16-byte salt from a supported high-quality source, through XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes before parsing or Expat's automatic generation.
assessment.target_route: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput creates root and namespace parsers, then calls ParseOneInput, which derives an unsigned-long SipHash value from the input, calls XML_SetHashSalt, and calls XML_Parse. It later creates, parses, and frees two child parsers.
assessment.failure_condition: For a finite valid XML input whose derived salt is nonzero, XML_SetHashSalt sets the upper key word to zero, writes only the unsigned-long value to the lower word, and sets the salt flag. XML_Parse therefore skips automatic full-salt generation, and internal hashing uses the limited key.
assessment.alternative_paths: The namespace parser uses the same helper. Children inherit the parent's salt and flag and also use that helper. No parser route calls XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes. A zero derived salt can leave automatic generation available, but it does not satisfy the full-salt requirement for the nonzero-salt condition assessed here.
